description: Exactness gate: run the inline esm-spec 6.6.5 tests of problems/divergence_mpas.esm (model Divergence, test div_of_curl_is_zero) on the icosahedral level-0 mesh (12 cells / 30 edges / 20 vertices) through each binding's official simulation pathway. The TRiSK mimetic identity div(curl) = 0 makes u(t) = u(0) exact to rounding: the assertions pin ic preservation (relative L2 of u vs the ic field, 0 at t=0 within 1e-12 and at t=1 within 1e-9), conservation (mean(u) = 6.5 within 1e-9), and the rule output itself (div_flux max/min = 0 within 1e-11, asserted DIRECTLY on the array observed -- the 6.6.5 observed-assertion form, evaluated by the Julia and Python runners through run_pde_tests' BuildInspection-backed observed-field paths). The assertions and their tolerances live in the problem file itself; this manifest only routes the runners. This is the repo's ragged-evaluation gate: the fv_divergence_cell rule body contracts over the ragged edges_of_cell index set ({from, of} with the nEdgesOnCell CSR offsets factor, esm-spec 4.3.1), the mesh data arrives as const-op subsystem observeds re-exposed as bare-name aliases (the MPAS keyed-factor wiring contract), and flux is a general edge-indexed aggregate observed -- all three capabilities landed in EarthSciSerialization.jl tree_walk (aggregate array-observed inlining; const-op/alias observed materialization; ragged dynamic bounds in expression-position aggregate expansion with model-scope keyed-factor resolution) for this case.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no aggregate lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no aggregate lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: earthsci-toolkit-rs cannot evaluate this case regardless of the §6.6.5 inline-test pathway's status: it has no ragged {from, of} index-set range evaluation (the per-cell CSR bound index(nEdgesOnCell, i) from the edges_of_cell registry entry), no general aggregate array-observed inlining (the edge-indexed flux and the div_flux rule output), no bare-alias/const-op keyed-factor materialization for the mesh subsystem re-exposure, and no assertion support for an OBSERVED target (div_flux max/min). Unblocks with a ragged CSR-offsets range expansion + observed-field evaluation in the array simulator (mirror of the 2026-07 Julia tree_walk ragged/keyed-factor/observed-assertion work).
